_comment: AI players (Homestead's own). The AI knows the whole map. Every thinkSeconds it starts at most one building: the first entry of buildOrder whose count it has not reached and which it can place (enough free planks and stones, a fitting spot on own land). After the food chain (pig farm, slaughterhouse) comes the big temple and the people's mana chain with a small temple; gold (Egyptians: gems too) for the combat strength comes late, where the land has it. A building that processes a mine's output (iron melt, gold melt) waits for an own mine of it or its ore on the own land (start goods). Entries that need a resource (trees, stones, ore, river, fish, swampy ground for rice) are skipped while the own land lacks it - the expansion then builds towers towards it.
_housingComment: A living house is started when fewer carriers than freeCarriers are available (residents still to come count as available), or while there are no more carriers than carriersPerProductionBuilding per production building (sites included), or when fewer than houseWhenConvertible carriers may still become specialists (recruitment.keptCarriers in production.json). Towers then leave its material.
_spareRoomComment: Living space no one needs (carriers turned soldiers): a living house that has released all its residents is torn down for its material when, without it, at least spareRoom places would still be left over and no house is wanted. The biggest such house goes first.
_foresterComment: Every checkSeconds the AI stops each forester with at least maxTrees trees (saplings too) in its work area and restarts the others. The forester entries of the build order are only a limit: one is built (within 12 fields) next to a finished woodcutter with fewer than buildBelowTrees trees (saplings too) in its work area and no forester whose work area takes in the woodcutter, one at a time (the last one must be working), or at home while there is no woodcutter (no trees on the own land).
_minesComment: A mine goes only where its chance per run (ore left within its radius against full fields, see resources.fullAmount in production.json) is at least minChance; with no such spot the AI expands towards more ore. A finished mine whose chance fell below abandonChance is torn down (after a while), so the next one goes where the ground is richer.
_houseSizesComment: Which living house: the first of houseSizes whose sawmills and stonecutters (finished) the player has, otherwise house. Per people below, after what their houses cost (Egyptians build with stone, Asians and Amazons with planks).
_stockComment: A storehouse is built only once the AI makes or owns gold bars or gems (a gold melt or gems mine works, or some lie on its land or in its buildings, taken over too) and stockWhenWaiting units of goods worth storing (storage.materials in production.json: tools, weapons, gold, gems) lie around and the storehouses have fewer than two free piles.

growth._comment: After the build order the economy keeps growing where it is short. Every think the AI notes what each finished, staffed building does; after windowSeconds a good that one kind of its consumers waited for at least starved of the time (per kind: weaponsmiths waiting for iron say nothing about the coal the iron melts lack), with fewer than inStock units in stock, gets one more producer (the kind the player has most of, else the first in the build order) - a workshop or mine only while the ones there are busy at least busy of the time, otherwise the shortage lies further up the chain. So the chain grows by itself: weaponsmith waiting for iron - iron melt, the melts waiting for ore - iron mine, the mines waiting for food - food. Weaponsmiths busy at least busy of the time get one more, barracks too while weaponsInStock weapons wait. One of a kind at a time: none while one is a site, nor when one was finished during the window. What the build order brings anyway is left to it. windowSeconds 0: no growth.

_expansionComment: Towers towards what the own land lacks, in this order: quarry stone below minStoneUnits, none of the listed ores, free building land below minFreeLand, stone below wantedStoneUnits, trees below minTrees, no river (waterworks draw from rivers only); towards free land when a building found no room; with spareSoldiersForLand idle soldiers and landStock planks and stones beyond the tower's cost simply towards the nearest free land. The tower goes to the own-land spot nearest the target. While a needed tower cannot be afforded, the economy keeps its planks and stones back.

expansion._minFreeLandComment: Free building land (grass points with nothing on them and no building around) the own land should keep; below it the AI expands towards the cells with the most of it.
expansion._lateOresComment: Towers towards these only late: once every build order entry before the mine of the ore is reached (houses and the mana chain come first), after all other needs except plain land.
expansion._maxWaterShareComment: Largest share of water (sea, lakes, rivers) among the unclaimed points a tower would take. Spots with more are passed over; towards a needed resource (stone, ore, trees, water) the spot with the least water is taken if none is below.

_magicComment: Priests follow the soldiers out on a strike or campaign and stay priestDistance fields behind them (towards home); otherwise they wait at home. A priest casts its spell where own soldiers fight or are out on a strike or campaign once the mana is there and at least minTargets soldiers not yet hit would be (own ones for a haste spell).

magic._upgradeComment: Soldier upgrades (magic.json, upgrades) are made as soon as enough mana has been earned in all (they spend none), in upgradeOrder (all to level 2, then the same order to level 3).
magic._turnComment: A strike or campaign about to be given up (too weak) is turned with the people's spell first while its soldiers still have turnRatio of what they would need: a priest freezes (converts, scatters) the enemies there, and frozen soldiers count nothing in the balance. Several priests cast at once on different parts of a fight, each where most soldiers not yet hit stand (enemy bowmen and reinforcements near the own soldiers too); frozen ones are frozen again just before they thaw. 0: never.

military._comment: Idle soldiers outside buildings, weighed every thinkSeconds; soldiers walking on a plain move order of the AI (to a post, home) count as idle, so their order is weighed again as well. The AI knows where every enemy soldier and geologist is. Enemies within groupRadius of each other form a group (geologists do not fight: one soldier is enough against them). Guerilla comes before holding soldiers back: a group within strikeRange of an own military building is attacked by the nearest idle soldiers once they have strikeRatio times its strength (health x damage per second), also by those that would otherwise stay back against it; only soldiers needed against the other groups within threatRange (strikeRatio times their strength) are kept out. An attack on the land (enemies walking or fighting) is met anywhere; enemies just standing around only if they stand at most hinterlandDepth fields deep in their own land (0: anywhere). The other idle soldiers are placed by the character's traits (guarding): guardByThreat shares them out by how strong and close the enemy groups within threatRange are, without any threat they gather at home; frontTowers, everyOtherTower and rotatingTowers spread them over the towers while there is no threat. A soldier within guardDistance of its post stays. reinforceRadius: enemy soldiers outside within this distance of a strike's target count as its defence too (scattered soldiers come to help; checked at the start and every think while it runs). towerFireRatio: guerilla (not defence) only where the bowmen of enemy military buildings reaching the target or the way are at most this times the enemies' strength – they cannot be struck back, losses to them win nothing (a lone soldier next to a full castle is left alone); a running guerilla strike whose enemies retreat under such fire is called off (0: no limit). Without such a trait they stay where they are.

wounded._comment: Small fights (strikes and campaigns with at most maxSoldiers own soldiers): a fighting soldier below withdrawHealth of its full health withdraws to restDistance fields from the enemies (beyond their sight) and holds its position – or, with an own hospital within its call range (not nearer the enemies), walks to its door, free to be healed (soldiers holding their position are not called) while the others still fighting have holdRatio times the enemy's strength without it. The withdrawn come back once healed to rejoinHealth, when those fighting fall below needRatio times the enemy's strength, or when the enemy has at most mopUpRatio times their strength left. withdrawHealth 0: never.

hospital._comment: Wounded soldiers: below woundedHealth of their full health. Idle ones go to the nearest own hospital at most sendDistance away: the weakest to its heal spot (who stands there is healed without being called), the others wait a few fields out in front of the door for their turn. More than wounded of them (not counting those still fighting a strike or campaign) further than sendDistance from every own hospital (sites too): a hospital is built at the own military building nearest them, before the build order (like living houses). wounded 0: never.

army._comment: Late game: a big army of lateSoldiers soldiers outside the buildings or more (its fights are too big to pull single wounded out, see military.wounded). Then the weaponsmiths make mostly spears and bows (lateShares, as in Waren > Herstellung): pikemen wear armour, bowmen shoot from behind them. Below three quarters of lateSoldiers the shares from before come back. 0: never.

attack._comment: Campaigns against enemy land. Defence comes first: idle soldiers needed against enemies near the own land stay back, and no campaign starts while enemies stand on the own land. Target: an occupied enemy military building; its defence is its garrison plus enemy soldiers within defenseRadius. Preferred are targets close to the own land, weakly defended, with no enemy group within pathClearance of the way there. A campaign starts when the spare soldiers have ratio times the target's defence and the AI's whole army has armyRatio (default: ratio; 0: any) times that enemy's (at least minSoldiers). commit (0-1, default 0): that share of the spare soldiers left over comes along as well (1: full strength). The soldiers first gather at the own military building nearest the target (at most gatherSeconds); the campaign is given up when they then have less than abortRatio (default: ratio; 0: never) times the defence, otherwise they attack together; they retreat when they fall below military.retreatRatio (0: never), and go home when it is over. maxDistance (default 0: any): targets at most this far from the own land (an enemy building at the border stands some 30 fields behind the edge of its land).
attack._garrisonWeightComment: Per building name: its garrison counts this many times in the defence (others once). A castle's soldiers are much harder to get at (one fighter at the door, bowmen on the roofs).

_characterComment: Characters (docs/KI-TACTICS.md): traits on top of the built-in behavior, in order of priority. A character may override a trait's settings under the trait's name and any general value (after the people's), e.g. "general": { "traits": ["pincer"], "pincer": { "feintShare": 0.5 } }. buildOrderMoves (building: places, negative = earlier) shifts every entry of a building in the people's build order. Made-up characters for trying out (arena, tournament): traits joined by '+' (pincer+guardByThreat), and @path=value on top of a character or traits (general@attack.ratio=1.3@buildOrderMoves.barrack=-5). characterWeights: which character a player gets, drawn once per game (per people under civilizations). The client and the arena can name it per player with --characters.

guardByThreat._comment: Idle soldiers guard the own military buildings by threat (values under military: threatRange, guardDistance).

pincer._comment: Pincer and feint: a campaign with at least minSoldiers is split. feintShare of them gather at the own building nearest the target, the rest walk round in an arc to a staging point flankAngle degrees off that direction, flankDistance fields from the target (at least out of its bowmen's reach). When both are in place the feint attacks; strikeSeconds later the main force strikes from the side. The way round takes time: extraShare more of the spare soldiers come along, and the attack is only given up when they have become weaker than the defence (military.retreatRatio).

waves._comment: Calm phases of calmSeconds without campaigns alternate with waves of waveSeconds in which campaigns may start one after another; each phase up to jitter (share) longer or shorter. Defence and guerilla go on.

frontGarrison._comment: Military buildings within frontDistance of an enemy military building (sites too) are fully staffed, the others get backline soldiers; the rest come out and are free for strikes and campaigns.

earlyArmy._comment: The first build order entries of buildings move together, in that order, right behind the first after entries (wood and stone): the start goods (iron ore, coal) become soldiers instead of waiting for mines and food. An iron melt may be built while iron ore lies on the own land, without a mine.

frontTowers._comment: Without a threat, idle soldiers are shared out evenly among the own military buildings facing the enemy: the nearest enemy military building can be reached without a detour (the way at most detour times the straight distance plus 5 fields) and without passing another own military building. Rechecked every checkSeconds. With a threat the next trait (guardByThreat) places them.

everyOtherTower._comment: Without a threat, idle soldiers are shared out evenly among every other own military building: bigger groups, quick at the neighbors left out. Front first; a building is left out when a neighbor of it (at most neighborFactor times the distance to the nearest one) is taken. With a threat the next trait (guardByThreat) places them.

rotatingTowers._comment: Without a threat, idle soldiers are shared out evenly among a random share of the own military buildings, drawn anew every rotateSeconds. With a threat the next trait (guardByThreat) places them.

forwardBase._comment: Idle soldiers gather at the own military building nearest an enemy one, as a base for guerilla strikes. When the enemy groups within military.threatRange of it are stronger than fallBackRatio times them, they fall back (without fighting on the way) to the own military building nearest the base that lies fallBackDistance fields further from those enemies (otherwise home); an enemy moving on is fought by defence and guerilla from behind. Takes the decision point guarding: comes before guardByThreat in a character.

thief._comment: Keeps scouts scouts (free carriers become ones) and sends them for goods at the edge of enemy land: piles on another player's land at most edgeDepth fields from where it ends (a storehouse right at the border has its piles some 8 fields in), within maxDistance of the own land, no enemy soldier outside the buildings within soldierRadius (one coming that near the scout or his pile calls him home; that pile is left alone for retrySeconds). Lost scouts are replaced at most every replaceSeconds (carriers are worth something too). ranks: goods best first (gold, gems, weapons, ores; then tools; then food; the rest last); the scout takes the best good around the pile. Loaded scouts walk to the nearest field of the own land and drop the goods there. Rechecked every checkSeconds. Errands only: combines with any other trait.

formation._comment: Bowmen first, melee behind (decision point leading fights): a strike with bowmen and melee soldiers against enemies mostly on foot (their bowmen at most maxEnemyBowShare of their strength), still at least the bowmen's range away, sends the bowmen ahead to shoot from range and parks the melee soldiers parkDistance fields behind them (beyond the enemies' sight: they wait). When an enemy comes within fallBackDistance of a bowman, the bowmen fall back without fighting behind the melee soldiers and these go in; later too, whenever an enemy gets that close again (at most every fallBackSeconds). After screenSeconds without that the melee soldiers go in anyway.

summoner._comment: Mana beyond reserveSpells casts of the people's own spell goes into summoning goods (magic.json, SummonGoods): a free priest casts it on the best spot within priestRadius of him – own land at least edgeDistance fields from where it ends (thieves, enemies; the map border does not count), no enemy soldier outside within soldierRadius, at least minFreeFields free fields (walkable, no pile, no building) within the spell radius; the most free fields win, then the nearest to the priest. Only while no priest of the player is casting. Rechecked every checkSeconds. Errands only: combines with any other trait.

characters._peoplesComment: One character per people (characterWeights under civilizations), each a recognisable opponent. Egyptians (hothead): hot-tempered, military early, attack at slight superiority with all they have, thin garrisons in the back. Asians (unyielding): hardly ever give up or retreat (only below half the defence; never at all bled them out). Romans (legion): strong economy with early gold, attack bundled in waves, pincers. Amazons (skirmisher): play safe at home (garrisons full, campaigns only at 2:1), but wear the enemy down with guerilla groups far out (at 2:1, so they do not turn round at the first sign of danger); campaigns only near the own land (an outpost far away is lost again). Idle soldiers without a threat: hothead keeps them in one heap at home, unyielding on a changing third of its towers, legion and general on every other tower, skirmisher on the towers facing the enemy; enemies standing around deep in their own land are left alone by the skirmisher (that mostly goes wrong). In fights legion, general and skirmisher send their bowmen ahead (formation); the hothead never pulls its wounded out.

civilizations._comment: Values per people, overriding the ones above (objects are merged). Example: "Roman": { "attack": { "ratio": 1.3 } }. Build orders per people: Romans need wood and stone alike (the general one above: one of each first, a second of each a little later); Egyptians build with much stone and little wood (one sawmill, many stonecutters); Asians and Amazons use many planks (a second wood production early, a third away from the others in long games; one stonecutter at first).
